summary.title: How to Build DNS Server in X Programming Language
summary.one_liner: An introduction to what DNS does and a multi-language project for building a toy DNS server, starting with Node.js.
takeaways: DNS maps human-readable domain names to numerical IP addresses, acting as the phone book of the Internet.
DNS replaced the single centralised HOSTS.TXT file maintained by Stanford Research Institute, created by Paul Mockapetris in 1983.
DNS mappings are distributed across a hierarchy of authorities and zones, which the guide explains when covering the recursive resolver.
The project aims to implement a toy DNS server in multiple languages, with Node.js (JavaScript) first and Ruby second.
summary.summary: This page introduces the Domain Name System, explaining how it turns domain names like example.com into IP addresses and how it evolved from the older HOSTS.TXT file. It describes the distributed hierarchy of DNS authorities and zones, which the guide says it will cover in relation to the recursive resolver. The author presents the work as an educational project to implement a toy DNS server in several languages, with JavaScript (Node.js) as the first and Ruby as the second. The page lists "Guides" and "Resources" sections, but the page text shows no content under them.
